steps.text: Ask the patient to breathe through their mouth.
Listen to breath sounds with your stethoscope at each auscultation point, anterior and posterior chest.
Compare each side with the other.
Listen for quality, intensity and adventitious sounds.
If you hear stridor (a loud strangulating sound on inspiration, clearest over the trachea), get an immediate review by a senior doctor.

notes.text: Before you listen, LOOK: general appearance (facial expression, anxiety, agitation, position), ability to talk, colour (peripheral and central), position of the trachea, work of breathing, rate, rhythm, cough, orthopnoea.

Adventitious sounds. Wheeze: continuous, high-pitched, hissing (air through narrowed airways). Crackles: interrupted, non-musical (distal airways opening on inspiration and collapsing on expiration). Pleural friction rub: grating (thickened pleura rubbing; pleurisy secondary to pneumonia or pulmonary infarction). Stridor: upper airway obstruction, needs an immediate senior doctor review.
A silent chest may mean total peripheral airway obstruction. Treat it as a warning sign, not an improvement.
FEEL (palpation): lumps or abnormal structures, skin temperature, rise and fall of the chest, pain. Percussion notes: resonant, hyper-resonant, dull.
Only 'stridor' is marked critical here, because the source says it needs immediate senior review. The source does not say which steps an assessor treats as fail points.
